mainEntity.name: How much protein do I need per day?

acceptedAnswer.text: For people who strength-train, research supports 0.7–1.0 grams of protein per pound of body weight (1.6–2.2 g/kg) for muscle building and retention. During a calorie deficit (cutting), aiming for the higher end (1.0 g/lb) helps preserve lean mass. During a surplus (bulking), 0.8 g/lb is generally sufficient.

Macros is short for macronutrients — the three main categories of nutrients that provide calories: protein (4 cal/g), carbohydrates (4 cal/g), and fat (9 cal/g). Tracking macros rather than just total calories helps ensure you get enough protein for muscle growth while balancing energy from carbs and fats.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate my macros?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with your Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE), then adjust calories up or down based on your goal. Set protein first (typically 0.8–1.0 g per pound of body weight), then fat (around 25–30% of total calories), and fill the remainder with carbohydrates. This calculator handles all of that math for you.

mainEntity.name: Should I eat the same macros on rest days?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most people, keeping macros consistent every day is simpler and just as effective. Advanced athletes sometimes use carb cycling — eating more carbs on training days and fewer on rest days — but the total weekly intake matters more than daily fluctuations. Consistency beats complexity.
